name: Beginning and performing rites with 'oṃ tat sat'
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Rites of sacrifice, giving and austerity enjoined by rule begin with the utterance of 'oṃ' (as among the expounders of brahman); seekers of release perform them with 'tat', without aiming at the fruit; 'sat' is applied to praiseworthy acts, steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving, and action for that purpose. The text gives no further procedure.

warnings.text: What is offered, given or done without faith is 'asat' and of no worth here or hereafter.

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Do sacrifice, giving and austerity — and prescribed action generally — because they ought to be done, giving up attachment and the fruit (18.5–6, 18.9); this is sāttvic relinquishment; the one who gives up the fruit is the true relinquisher, since action cannot be given up entirely (18.11).

warnings.text: Giving up prescribed action out of delusion is tāmasic relinquishment.
Giving up action as painful, from fear of bodily hardship, is rājasic and does not bring the fruit of relinquishment.

name: Austerity of body, speech and mind
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Bodily austerity: worship of gods, twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy, non-harm. Verbal: non-agitating, true, pleasant and beneficial speech, and practice of recitation. Mental: serenity, gentleness, silence, self-restraint, purity of disposition (17.14–16). Practised with highest faith by the yoked who do not desire fruit it is sāttvic (17.17).

warnings.text: Austerity done for respect, honour and show is rājasic, unstable and impermanent.
Austerity from a deluded notion, with self-torment or to ruin another is tāmasic.
Terrible austerity not enjoined by scripture, with hypocrisy and egoism, tormenting the elements of the body and the Lord within, is of demonic resolve.

name: Austerity (tapas)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Austerity is threefold, of body, speech and mind (17.14–16); with sacrifice and giving it is not to be given up, being a purifier of the wise, but done without attachment and fruit (18.5–6).

warnings.text: Terrible austerity not enjoined by scripture, joined with hypocrisy and egoism, that torments the body and the Lord within it, is of demonic resolve.
Austerity performed with self-torment or for another's ruin is tāmasic.

name: Sāttvic food
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Foods dear to the sāttvic are those that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and delight, and are savoury, rich, lasting and heart-pleasing (17.8).

warnings.text: Pungent, sour, salty, very hot, sharp, dry and burning foods, dear to the rājasic, bring pain, grief and disease.
Spoiled, tasteless, putrid, stale, leftover and impure food is dear to the tāmasic.

name: Giving (dāna)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Give because it ought to be given, to one who makes no return, at the right place and time, to a fit recipient (17.20); giving is not to be given up (18.5).

warnings.text: Giving for a return, with an eye to fruit, or grudgingly is rājasic.
Giving at the wrong place and time, to the unfit, without respect and with contempt is tāmasic.

name: Sacrifice and eating its remains (yajña, yajña-śiṣṭa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Offer sacrifice as seen in the rule, without desire for fruit, with the mind settled on 'it ought to be offered' (17.11); begin it with 'oṃ' (17.24); do not give it up but do it without attachment and fruit (18.5–6).

warnings.text: Sacrifice aimed at fruit or for show is rājasic.
Sacrifice without rule, food distributed, mantras, fee or faith is tāmasic.
The demonic sacrifice in name only, with hypocrisy, not according to rule.

name: Performing one's own dharma (svadharma)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Devoted to one's own action (sva-karman), worship with it the one from whom beings proceed and by whom all is pervaded, and so attain perfection (18.45–46); one's own dharma, though deficient, is better than another's well done (18.47); do not give up the action one is born to even if faulty (18.48).
stage: the first step of the sequence of 18.45–56

name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Renounce in thought all actions to Kṛṣṇa, intent on him, resorting to the yoga of understanding, with thought ever on him (18.57); so one crosses all difficulties by his grace (18.58).

warnings.text: If out of ego one will not listen, one perishes.

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Go to the Lord in the heart alone for refuge with one's whole being; by his grace one attains supreme peace and the eternal abode (18.62). The most secret word: relinquishing all dharmas, come to Kṛṣṇa alone for refuge; he will free you from all evils; do not grieve (18.66).

name: Study and hearing of the Gītā
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Teaching the supreme secret to devotees, with supreme devotion, leads to Kṛṣṇa, and none is dearer to him (18.68–69); studying the dialogue is worship by the sacrifice of knowledge (18.70); even hearing it with faith and without cavilling brings, freed, the worlds of the meritorious (18.71).
prerequisites: The hearer should have austerity and devotion, wish to listen and not cavil at Kṛṣṇa (18.67).

warnings.text: It is never to be told to one without austerity, without devotion, unwilling to listen, or who cavils at Kṛṣṇa.

name: The Gītā's meditation (dhyāna-yoga, BhG 6.10–32)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: In the account of how the perfected one attains brahman: frequent solitude, eat lightly, restrain speech, body and mind, be ever intent on the yoga of meditation and rest on dispassion (18.52), with purified understanding, self-restraint by steadfastness and giving up of sense-objects, passion and aversion (18.51), and the casting off of ego, force, arrogance, desire, anger and possession (18.53).
signs_of_progress: having become brahman: serene, neither grieving nor desiring, the same to all beings (18.54)

name: Karma-yoga: performing one's duty without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Do prescribed action without attachment, without passion or aversion and without desire for the fruit (18.23); the doer free of attachment and 'I'-talk, steadfast and zealous, unchanged in success and failure is sāttvic (18.26).
